## Multi-Source AI News Briefing
A production-grade daily briefing. It pulls AI news from Hacker News, dev.to and Lobste.rs, normalizes the three feeds into one schema, drops stories already sent in previous runs, scores what is left by engagement, recency and AI-topic relevance, and takes the top N. OpenAI then works as news editor: it groups stories into categories, writes a one-line summary plus a why-it-matters note per story, and opens with an executive take. The briefing is formatted as Telegram Markdown, split into safe-sized chunks, and delivered to your chat.

### How it works
1. The schedule trigger runs daily at 08:00; the manual trigger is for testing.
2. The Configuration node holds every setting: query, story count, lookback window, AI model, briefing title, Telegram chat ID.
3. Three HTTP nodes fetch Hacker News, dev.to and Lobste.rs in parallel, each with retries. A failed source is skipped, never fatal.
4. Merge, Normalize, Deduplicate (via workflow static data) and Score turn three feeds into one ranked list.
5. If nothing is fresh, a short status note goes out and the AI call is skipped.
6. OpenAI must return strict JSON (executive take plus categorized stories). Any model failure or bad JSON degrades to a headlines-only briefing.
7. The briefing is Markdown-escaped, split into 4000-char chunks, sent to Telegram, and sent URLs are persisted so they are never resent.

### Setup
- Create a Telegram bot with @BotFather and copy the token. Get your chat ID via @userinfobot.
- Add an OpenAI API key as credentials on the Analyze with AI node, and Telegram credentials on the Send Telegram Briefing node.
- Paste your chat ID into the Configuration node, test with the manual trigger, then activate.

### 1 - Triggers and configuration
The schedule runs the briefing daily at 08:00. Use the manual trigger to test any time. Every tunable lives in the Configuration node: query, story count, lookback window, AI model, briefing title, Telegram chat ID.

### 2 - Ingest from three sources
Hacker News (Algolia), dev.to and Lobste.rs are fetched in parallel. Each fetch retries twice; a failed source returns an error item that the normalizer skips, so one dead source never kills the run.

### 3 - Normalize, deduplicate, score
The three feeds become one story schema. URLs already sent in previous runs are dropped via workflow static data. Remaining stories are scored by engagement x recency decay x AI-keyword boost, then ranked.

### 4 - AI analysis with fallback
OpenAI acts as news editor and must return strict JSON: an executive take plus categorized stories with one-liners. Any model failure or unparseable output degrades to a headlines-only briefing instead of crashing the run.

messages.content: You are a senior tech news editor. Return only valid JSON, no markdown fences, no commentary. Plain language, no hype, no emojis.

parameters.content:
### 5 - Format and deliver
The briefing is formatted as Telegram Markdown with escaping, split into 4000-char chunks (Telegram caps messages at 4096). Each chunk is sent, then sent URLs are persisted so the next run never resends them.

### Warnings
- Any single source can fail or rate-limit: each fetch has retries and a failed source is skipped, not fatal.
- Deduplication uses workflow static data, which only persists on ACTIVE workflows. Manual test runs always see the full feed.
- Telegram caps messages at 4096 chars: the formatter splits into 4000-char chunks automatically.
- The OpenAI step costs a few cents per run on gpt-4o-mini. Change the model in the Configuration node.
- Never commit real credentials, chat IDs or API keys into this workflow JSON.
